brief: A wall clock with hands that turn and tell the time.

requirements.evidence: The catalog has no clock face, dial, movement, or wall-clock kit. Searches for clock, hand, dial, rotate, pivot, spindle and gear returned only a rod socket accessory, bins, notches and hex bases. I placed nothing, so the build is still a single empty hex base.

No hand or pointer part and no motor or rotating joint exists in the catalog. The only free-spinning part is a filament spool on a spool axle between two rod sockets. A spool is not a clock hand and would not show time, so I did not substitute it.
Depends on the two items above. Props (174 found) include tools, plants and workshop items but nothing that marks hour or minute positions.

finish.summary: I did not build the wall clock. Hex Cluster is a modular hardware system with bases, bins, covers, rod sockets, spool axles and spikes, but nothing that makes a clock: no dial, no hour or minute hands, and no motor or rotating joint for hands to turn on. The closest parts are a spool on a spool axle, which spins freely, but a spool is not a clock hand and would not tell the time, so I left it out. The configurator checks fit and collisions only, so it cannot make a timekeeping mechanism. Nearest buildable alternative: a static wall-mounted hex panel with a rod-socket pivot for a hand, or a hanging spool used as a decorative disc. Neither would meet the brief's requirements, so I did not build either without your go-ahead.
